column1: #               the medieval tradition
#   work        author and title as usually cited
#   columns     total columns of the ORIGINAL roll. Blank if unknown.
#   stichoi     total stichoi if an ancient count survives. Blank if unknown.
#   height_cm   roll height (page height). Blank if unknown.
#   diam_cm     original roll diameter. Blank if unknown.
#   status      measured | reconstructed | population | attested | assumed
#   source      where the number comes from. NEVER leave this blank.
# RULES OF ENTRY
#   1. No number without a source. An empty cell is information; an invented
#      cell is damage.
#   2. `columns` is the preferred size unit. The chain
#      columns -> sheet length -> diameter uses only the column period
#      is the more reliable of the two horizontal grid numbers.
#      Going through `stichoi` for PROSE additionally requires the letter
#      pitch (a stichos is a notional 35-letter unit
#      and the letter pitch is currently under suspicion — see
#      data_sources.md. For VERSE a stichos IS the physical line and the
#      chain stays clean.
#   3. Distinguish the roll as it survives from the roll as it was. Several
#      Herculaneum rolls lost most of their bulk to 18th-20th century opening
#      attempts; PHerc. 1667 went from 4.9 cm to 2 cm of diameter that way.
# PRIOR ART — this is not a new idea. Papyrologists reconstruct original roll
# length and column counts from the width of successive volutions on opened
# fragments (e.g. the reconstruction of PHerc. 1004
# On Rhetoric
